findings.evidence: GStack's round-trip claim stopped at '/api/frontend/wheel/config returned 200' and explicitly did not click spin/claim — that only proves the CONFIG read path works, not the gameplay write path (spin draw, claim persistence, prize award, account creation). I pushed further SAFELY: wrapped a direct call to WheelUnlockService::issue() -> WheelStepService::open()x2 (backdated dwell timestamps, since that timer is an anti-fraud control unrelated to what's being tested) -> WheelService::drawPending() -> WheelService::claimPending() inside DB::beginTransaction()/DB::rollBack() with Mail::fake() to suppress the real WheelPrizeMail send. Result: real weighted draw returned {"key":"cheeseburger","type":"free_item"}, WheelSpin id 4180 persisted with award() logic executing cleanly, then verified via tinker that App\Models\WheelSpin::find(4180) and the seeded email both return NO ROWS post-rollback (CONFIRMED_ROLLED_BACK_CLEAN / NO_USER_LEAK). This is materially stronger evidence than a 200 on /config and closes most of the depth gap GStack left open.
findings.fix_hint: Not a code fix — a report-writing fix. GStack's Wave D report should not have characterized '/config returns 200, segments render' as proving the round-trip 'worked' without qualifying that gameplay (spin/claim) was unverified. Recommend the standing playbook for this kind of check become: exercise the real service methods inside a rolled-back DB::transaction() + Mail::fake(), exactly as done here — it is safe (verified zero residue) and far more convincing than a config-only check. Residual gap even after this: the actual browser-side fetch() calls for spin/claim across the live 8899->8000 cross-origin boundary were still never clicked by anyone. This is very likely fine (config/cors.php paths=['api/*'] covers the whole API surface including spin/claim, allowed_origins_patterns explicitly matches any localhost/127.0.0.1 port including 8899, and roue.html uses one shared fetch(API + chemin) wrapper for config/step/spin/claim alike — verified at roue.html:555,999) but that is inference from code reading, not an observed click-through, and should be labeled as such rather than as 'proven live'.

findings.evidence: Traced the name 'Dorian' cited in GStack's 'Content de te revoir, Dorian !' DOM snippet. It does NOT match the only known localStorage-seeding fixture for that exact screen (tests-e2e/account-retour-connu-2026-08-13.spec.js seeds FIRST='Julie', PHONE='0612345678' — confirmed by reading the spec). 'Dorian' does NOT appear anywhere in the static web repo except as an unrelated placeholder attribute on roue.html:515 (`placeholder="Dorian"` on the name input, decorative ghost text, never persisted). It DOES appear as a recurring test-customer name across several backend PHPUnit fixtures (tests/Feature/Wheel/WheelClaimAccountTest.php, WheelDrawSecurityTest.php, WheelHistoryTest.php, tests/Feature/Promo/PromoFlyerTicketLayoutTest.php) — a plausible coincidental reuse, not proof either way. Because no DOM/console/network artifact for that screen exists (see D-001), I cannot determine whether this reflects a genuinely fresh, isolated test run or contamination from a shared browser profile/localStorage across the 4 concurrent Wave A-D agents mentioned in the mission brief. account-retour-connu-2026-08-13.spec.js itself uses correct isolation (`chromium.launch()` fresh incognito context per run); the risk is specifically if Wave D used a persistent/shared Chrome profile (e.g. an interactive extension-driven session) instead.
findings.fix_hint: Re-run the exact scenario that produced the Dorian greeting with a fresh incognito `chromium.launch()` context (not a shared/reused browser profile) and save the .dom.html + a `localStorage` dump alongside the screenshot, so the seed origin is traceable. Until then, treat this specific DOM claim as unverified rather than confirmed.

findings.evidence: Confirmed Debugbar is active on this route in local dev: `config('debugbar.enabled')` resolves to `env('DEBUGBAR_ENABLED', null)` -> null -> follows APP_DEBUG, and .env has APP_DEBUG=true; no `Debugbar::disable()` call found in WheelCounterController@kiosk. So the claim 'Debugbar is present in tab order' is accurate. However the framing 'zero real focusable elements, only Debugbar' undersells that Laravel Debugbar's own toolbar DOES inject genuinely tabbable `<a>` elements (its tab UI) — those are real, reachable tab-stops for a keyboard user on this screen today, not inert noise. That said, GStack's dismissal as dev-only is directionally correct for the audit's purpose: config/debugbar.php hard-disables it in production (`'enabled' => $isProduction ? false : ...`, verified), so this specific instance cannot reach production regardless of APP_DEBUG drift. Whether a fully keyboard-inert kiosk display (0 focusable elements once Debugbar is excluded) is itself acceptable depends on whether staff ever need keyboard-only recovery on this tablet — plausibly fine for a passive customer-facing display, but not verified either way.
findings.fix_hint: No code fix required for production. If this needs re-checking, do it with APP_DEBUG=false locally (matching prod parity) rather than accepting Debugbar's tab-stops as the answer to 'is the real kiosk UI keyboard-navigable end to end'.
